canonical_status: Claim settled. Payment sent via NEFT.
aliases: Claim settled. Payment sent via NEFT
Claim settled. Amount credited via NEFT
Your claim has been settled and payment sent via NEFT
Claim settled payment sent via NEFT on
Claim Settled. Payment sent via NEFT
meaning: EPFO has processed and approved your claim. The payment has been dispatched electronically (NEFT) to your registered bank account. Settlement is complete on EPFO's side — the funds are now in the banking system.
action_required: Log in to your bank account or UAN portal to verify that the credited amount matches what you expected. If the amount has not appeared in 3–4 working days after the settlement date shown on the portal, contact your bank's customer care with the NEFT UTR reference number visible on the EPFO portal.
dont_do_this: Do not re-submit the claim — it has already been settled. Do not raise a fresh grievance on EPFO IGMS at this stage; any delay now is a banking clearance issue, not an EPFO processing issue.
typical_next_stage: Completed — no further action required on EPFO portal once bank credits the amount.
wait_guidance: NEFT credits typically clear within 1–3 working days from the date shown on the portal. If not credited after 4 working days, contact your bank — not EPFO.

canonical_status: Claim submitted. Under process at employer.
aliases: Claim submitted under process at employer
Claim submitted. Under process at employer
Claim is under process at employer
Claim is pending at employer end
meaning: Your claim has been submitted on the EPFO Member Portal and is currently waiting for your employer (HR / payroll department) to verify and digitally approve it. EPFO has not yet received the claim — the ball is entirely in your employer's court.
action_required: Contact your employer's HR or payroll department directly. Ask them to log in to the Employer EPFO portal and approve (attest) your pending claim. Provide them with your UAN number and the claim reference ID. Follow up in writing (email) so you have a timestamp trail.
dont_do_this: Do not contact EPFO helpline at this stage — they cannot act until the employer approves. Do not submit a second claim while this one is pending employer action; it will create duplicates and further delay processing.
typical_next_stage: EPFO Review — once the employer digitally approves, the claim moves into EPFO's internal queue.
wait_guidance: Employer attestation timelines vary widely depending on your HR department's responsiveness. There is no fixed regulatory deadline for this step; persistent, documented follow-up with your employer is the only lever you have.

aliases: Claim is being processed by EPFO
Claim received by EPFO. Under processing.
Under process at jurisdictional EPFO office
meaning: EPFO has received and accepted your claim from the employer and is now verifying it internally. This stage includes KYC checks, account balance verification, and scrutiny by the dealing assistant at the jurisdictional EPFO regional office.
action_required: No immediate action is required from your side. Monitor the status every 3–5 working days on the EPFO Member Portal or via the UMANG app. If the status has not changed for an unusually long period (see wait guidance), raise a grievance on the EPFO IGMS portal (epfigms.gov.in) referencing your claim ID.
dont_do_this: Do not call the EPFO helpline repeatedly on consecutive days — it will not accelerate processing and ties up lines for others. Do not submit a fresh claim; a duplicate will be rejected and will restart the clock. Do not approach any intermediary or 'agent' who offers to speed up EPFO processing for a fee.
typical_next_stage: Decision — EPFO will either approve the claim (moving to Payment), reject it, or return it for correction.
wait_guidance: Processing timelines depend on the jurisdictional office's workload and the claim type. PF full settlement claims (Form 19) are meant to be processed within 20 days of receipt. Pension claims (Form 10C/D) may take longer. If the status has not progressed after 30 days, file an IGMS grievance.

canonical_status: Pending for approval at field office.
aliases: Pending for approval at field office
Pending for approval at EPFO field office
Claim pending for approval at field office
meaning: Your claim has been processed internally at EPFO and is now in the final approval queue at the jurisdictional field (regional) office. A dealing assistant or the Assistant PF Commissioner is reviewing it before final sign-off. This is a normal stage just before settlement.
action_required: No action required from your side at this moment — this is EPFO's internal approval step. Check back in 5–7 working days. If the status stays stuck here for more than 15 working days, raise a grievance on EPFO IGMS (epfigms.gov.in) with your claim ID.
dont_do_this: Do not submit a fresh claim — this one is in the final approval queue. Do not visit the EPFO office without first trying the IGMS grievance route, as walk-in visits for approval follow-up are generally not productive.
typical_next_stage: Approved, Payment Under Process — once the field officer approves, the payment instruction is issued.
wait_guidance: Field office approval can take 5–15 working days depending on the regional office's backlog. If the status does not move after 15 working days, file an IGMS grievance — this creates an audit trail that typically prompts faster action.

aliases: Claim approved and payment is under process
meaning: Your claim has been fully approved by the EPFO field office. The payment instruction has been issued and is currently being processed for NEFT transfer to your registered bank account. You are very close to receiving the funds.
action_required: No action required. Ensure your registered bank account is active and linked to your UAN with correct IFSC code. Check your bank account within 3–5 working days — the NEFT credit should arrive. You can also check the portal for a UTR number once the payment is dispatched.
dont_do_this: Do not submit a fresh claim — your claim is approved and payment is on the way. Do not change your registered bank account details now; modifying KYC mid-payment can cause a failed NEFT transaction.
typical_next_stage: Settled — once NEFT is credited, the status updates to settled/completed.
wait_guidance: NEFT dispatch from EPFO typically happens within 3–7 working days of the approved status appearing. If you see no credit after 7 working days, check the portal for a UTR number and raise a grievance on IGMS if the UTR is missing.

aliases: Rejected: see rejection remarks on portal
Your PF claim has been rejected
Claim rejected. Please re-submit with corrections.
Rejected: Name mismatch in Aadhaar vs UAN
meaning: EPFO has reviewed your claim and decided to reject it. A rejection reason (remarks) should be visible on the portal against this claim. Common reasons include KYC mismatch (name, DOB, Aadhaar), incorrect bank account details, insufficient service period, or duplicate/pending claims.
action_required: Read the rejection remarks carefully on the portal. Identify the exact reason. If it is a KYC mismatch, update your KYC details via your employer on the UAN portal and re-submit after correction. If it is a bank account issue, update your bank details and re-submit. If you believe the rejection is incorrect, file a grievance on EPFO IGMS (epfigms.gov.in) with documentary evidence.
dont_do_this: Do not re-submit the same claim without first resolving the stated rejection reason — it will be rejected again. Do not ignore a rejected claim; unclaimed PF remains in your account but pension corpus has deadlines.
typical_next_stage: You must re-submit with corrected information. There is no automatic appeal — re-submission is the mechanism.
wait_guidance: After correcting the underlying issue (KYC, bank details, documents), re-submit the claim. The re-submitted claim will re-enter the Employer Review → EPFO Review pipeline from the beginning.

meaning: EPFO has identified a correctable issue with your claim and returned it to you (or your employer) rather than outright rejecting it. This is less severe than a rejection — it indicates that the claim can proceed once the specific correction is made. The correction remarks on the portal will specify what needs to be fixed.
action_required: Review the correction remarks on the portal. Common corrections include: updating Aadhaar-linked mobile number, correcting the bank account IFSC, uploading a missing document, or asking your employer to re-attest with corrected service dates. Make the required change and re-submit the claim.
dont_do_this: Do not re-submit without making the specific correction mentioned in the remarks — it will be returned again. Do not confuse 'Returned for Correction' with 'Rejected' — you do not need to start a fresh claim; re-submission is sufficient.
typical_next_stage: EPFO Review — once the correction is made and the claim is re-submitted (and employer re-attests if required), it re-enters the EPFO processing queue.
wait_guidance: The sooner you make the correction and re-submit, the sooner processing resumes. Corrections that require employer attestation depend on your employer's availability; contact HR immediately.

canonical_status: Payment failed. Bank account details incorrect.
aliases: Payment failed bank account details incorrect
Payment failed due to incorrect bank details
Payment failed please update bank details
NEFT rejected due to IFSC mismatch
meaning: EPFO approved and dispatched your payment, but the bank rejected the NEFT transfer because the bank account number, IFSC code, or account name on your UAN profile does not match the bank's records. The money has been returned to EPFO's account and not credited to you.
action_required: Immediately update your bank account details on the UAN Member Portal (unifiedportal-mem.epfindia.gov.in) under 'Manage → KYC'. Ensure the account number, IFSC code, and the account holder name exactly match your bank records. Once KYC is updated and verified, contact your EPFO regional office or raise an IGMS grievance requesting re-initiation of the NEFT payment.
dont_do_this: Do not submit a fresh claim — the settlement is already done and the money is held at EPFO pending re-credit. Do not update bank details hastily with incorrect information — a second failed NEFT will delay you further.
typical_next_stage: Payment → Completed — once the bank details are corrected and EPFO re-initiates the NEFT, the credit should appear within 1–3 working days.
wait_guidance: After updating your KYC bank details, allow 3–7 working days for EPFO to verify and re-initiate the NEFT. If you do not hear back, follow up via IGMS with your claim ID and UAN.

meaning: Your PF advance claim (such as for medical emergency, housing, or pandemic relief) was processed through EPFO's auto-settlement system, which bypasses manual review for eligible claims. Payment has been dispatched electronically.
action_required: Check your registered bank account for the credited amount. Verify the amount against what you claimed. If the amount is incorrect or not received, raise a grievance on EPFO IGMS with your UAN, claim ID, and expected amount.
dont_do_this: Do not re-submit the advance claim — auto-settlement means it has already been processed. Note that some advance types have a cooling-off period before you can re-apply for the same purpose.
typical_next_stage: Completed — no further action required unless the bank credit does not arrive.
wait_guidance: Auto-settled advances are credited within 72 hours of the settlement status appearing on the portal, subject to banking clearance times.

meaning: You have successfully filed your claim on the EPFO Member Portal. The claim is now in the initial queue and has not yet been picked up or reviewed by your employer's administrator. This is the normal state immediately after submission.
action_required: Notify your employer HR or payroll team that you have submitted a claim and provide your UAN and claim reference. Ask them to log in to the Employer EPFO portal and process the attestation at the earliest.
dont_do_this: Do not submit the same claim again — you already have an active submission. Do not contact EPFO at this stage — employer attestation must happen first.
typical_next_stage: Employer Review — the status will update once the employer logs in and acts on the claim.
wait_guidance: There is no fixed system deadline for employer attestation after claim submission. Your employer's internal process determines the timeline; follow up proactively in writing.

canonical_status: Transfer claim pending at previous employer.
aliases: Transfer claim pending at previous employer
meaning: Your Form 13 transfer claim is currently pending verification and approval by your previous employer. Transfer claims must be attested by either your previous or present employer.
action_required: Contact the HR department of your previous employer to approve your transfer claim on the employer portal.
dont_do_this: Do not submit another transfer claim. Do not contact EPFO yet.
wait_guidance: Follow up with your previous employer.

canonical_status: Transfer claim pending at present employer.
aliases: Transfer claim pending at present employer
meaning: Your Form 13 transfer claim is currently pending verification and approval by your present employer.
action_required: Contact the HR department of your current employer to approve your transfer claim on the employer portal.
dont_do_this: Do not submit another transfer claim. Do not contact EPFO yet.
wait_guidance: Follow up with your present employer.

canonical_status: Transfer claim completed. Annexure K generated.
aliases: Transfer claim accepted. Annexure K generated
meaning: Your PF transfer claim (Form 13) has been successfully processed. Annexure K is the official document confirming the transfer of your PF accumulations and service details from your previous account to your current account.
action_required: Download Annexure K from the portal for your records. Check your current PF passbook to verify the transferred amount and service history are reflected.
dont_do_this: Do not raise any grievances unless the transferred amount does not reflect in your passbook after a few days.
wait_guidance: It may take a few days for the transferred balance to show up in your current passbook after Annexure K is generated.

aliases: Claim already settled for this member ID
meaning: The system has locked or rejected your claim because a similar claim is already in process, or you are trying to claim funds that have already been settled. The portal prevents multiple concurrent claims of the same type to prevent fraud and processing errors.
action_required: Check your claim status history. If a claim is already under process, wait for its completion. If it was already settled, check your bank account or passbook.
dont_do_this: Do not attempt to submit further claims of the same type until the pending one is resolved.
typical_next_stage: Rejected — no further action on this specific submission.
wait_guidance: Focus on tracking your original, pending claim.

meaning: The status text you pasted does not closely match any entry in the public EPFO status taxonomy this tool covers. This could be because the portal language has changed, the status is specific to a less common claim type, or the text contains a custom remark from a regional office.
action_required: For general guidance: (1) Call the EPFO toll-free helpline at 1800-118-005 (Monday–Saturday, 9 AM–6 PM). (2) Raise a grievance on EPFO IGMS (epfigms.gov.in) with your UAN, claim ID, and a description of the status shown. (3) Visit your jurisdictional EPFO office with your UAN passbook printout, claim reference, and ID proof.
dont_do_this: Do not re-submit a claim solely because you do not understand the status — get clarification first to avoid creating duplicate claims.
typical_next_stage: Unknown — manual clarification from EPFO is required before you can determine next steps.
wait_guidance: Seek manual clarification before assuming your claim is stalled. The status may be a normal intermediate state not covered by this tool's current taxonomy.
